title: 9B CPU-only vs CPU+GPU tandem: three controlled runs at 24,576
command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=6 KINDI_DEVICE=cpu python -m kindi --pack ~/.kindi/packs/bonsai-9b --ctx 24576 bench --split-at none --json cpu.json; OMP_NUM_THREADS=6 python -m kindi --pack ~/.kindi/packs/bonsai-9b --ctx 24576 bench --tandem cpu-first --tandem-cpu-layers 6 --sample-vram --split-at none --json tandem.json; then the same pair into cpu-2.json/tandem-2.json and cpu-3.json/tandem-3.json (one fresh process per placement; pair 3 after a passive >7 h cooldown)
notes: This is the controlled replacement for the old cross-run 9B tandem-to-CPU ratio. The 2B/4B rows remain one pair; the 9B row is the median of three fresh-process pairs. Run 3 reproduced run 2's tandem row within 8% and its CPU row within 4-10% at every CPU cell except 24K, where CPU-only 1.8 -> 2.4 tok/s (+33%), so run 2 was not a run-wide outlier; run 1 is the high side. The three-run median makes the shallow ratio 4.1x (range 3.0x-4.2x) and the 24K row 6.2x (per-run range 5.8x-8.2x). Run 1 verified 4/4 and 133/133 at both placements; runs 2-3 were throughput only. The full-GPU 9B rows remain the 2026-11-17 capacity run; pair 3 followed a passive >7 h idle cooldown at 32 C, not an instrumented thermal control.
